subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should the fix use a default bounded Docker/sandbox-prep timeout and fail-soft behavior, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91015 be completed or replaced to cover the full resolveSandboxContext path?
rationale: The source-backed bug remains, but choosing timeout defaults, config exposure, fail-soft semantics, and how much of prune/layout/hash/init must be covered is a maintainer product/compatibility decision rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Complete or replace the timeout PR
options.body: Refresh or replace the open PR so the full Docker control-plane prep path is bounded, current skills workspace behavior is preserved, docs/config expectations are clear, and redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof is attached.

options.title: Accept a narrower mitigation
options.body: Maintainers could deliberately land only a Docker exec/init timeout first, while leaving this issue open for prune/layout/user-resolution diagnostics and accepting that the cold-start report is only partially addressed.

options.title: Pause for live reproduction first
options.body: Maintainers could require the original logs or a fresh macOS/OrbStack cold-start repro before changing default timeout or fail-soft behavior.

recommendation.title: Complete or replace the timeout PR
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open PR so the full Docker control-plane prep path is bounded, current skills workspace behavior is preserved, docs/config expectations are clear, and redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox architecture, config/default compatibility, and product availability semantics, and history shows repeated work on those paths.
